name: Autologous dermal-fat flap buttock augmentation

card.summary: A surgical buttock lift that folds the patient's own dermal-fat tissue into the buttock to add projection and correct sagging in one operation, without implants.
card.note: Major surgery with an extended, concealable scar; published series are small and retrospective.

quick.overview:
Autologous dermal-fat flap augmentation is a plastic-surgery technique that reshapes and enlarges the buttocks using the patient's own skin-and-fat tissue. Instead of discarding excess tissue during a lift, the surgeon keeps it attached to its blood supply and repositions it to fill out the buttock.

A 2008 case series describes it as addressing both sagging and lack of volume, a combination where an isolated lift may flatten the contour and implants or fat injections alone may not correct the droop. Related dermal-fat flaps are used elsewhere in reconstructive surgery, including face and breast.
quick.how: It is done by a plastic surgeon under anesthesia as part of a buttock lift or lower body lift, with an incision that can be hidden by underwear or a bikini. Recovery involves the usual restrictions after body-contouring surgery. The details of the operation are surgical and are not covered here.
quick.risks: Documented risks of body-contouring and buttock surgery include wound problems, seroma, asymmetry, fat necrosis and scarring. The longest incision line is a recognised drawback. Published experience for this specific technique comes from small series, so complication rates are not well established.

lead: Autologous dermal-fat flap buttock augmentation is a form of gluteoplasty that uses the patient's own dermal-fat tissue to add volume and lift to the buttocks. In a 2008 Aesthetic Surgery Journal report, surgeons describe it as a buttock lift with dermal fat flap augmentation for patients who have both ptosis (sagging) and a volume deficit [1].

For appearance, it aims at a rounder, higher, better-projected buttock contour from one operation. The authors note that an isolated lift may leave a flattened contour, while implants or fat injection alone may not fix ptosis [1]. Wikipedia lists dermal-fat flap body contouring, combined with fat injection, among buttock augmentation approaches, and as an option after massive weight loss [2].

Dermal-fat flaps are an established tool elsewhere in surgery, from nipple reconstruction to breast-conserving surgery and facial defects [3][4][5], and a body-lift technique with a dermal fat flap was published in 2002 [6].

angle.text: The operation redistributes the patient's own tissue to add volume at the mid-level of the buttock while lifting it, so ptosis and flatness are addressed together.

paras: In this technique, tissue that would be excised in a lift is retained as a dermal-fat flap and used to augment the buttock, so volume is added without implants [1]. Wikipedia places it among body-contouring options for flat buttocks with ptosis and for lower body lifts after major weight loss [2].

Implants and fat grafting are the more common options. Wikipedia summarises a 2019 meta-analysis of 46 publications reporting a 7% complication rate for fat grafting versus 31% for implants, and notes risks such as resorption of grafted fat, asymmetry and seroma [2]. Fat grafting has been linked to deaths in some surgical series [2].

A retrospective review of 10 patients aged 26 to 57 who had a buttock lift with autologous dermal flap augmentation, followed for 6 months to 2 years, reported improved contour on photographs, maximum augmentation at the midlevel of the buttocks, no major or minor complications and high patient satisfaction; the authors list the long incision line, concealable by underwear or a bikini, as a drawback [1]. A 2002 paper describing a body lift with a dermal fat flap and trochanteric and buttock suspension reported shorter operating times through precise markings [6].

Studies of dermal-fat flaps in other regions give context for the tissue type. A case report used an abdominal dermal-fat flap to rebuild a cheek defect after radiotherapy [3]. A series of 1,476 breast surgery patients, mainly using pedicled fat flaps, graded fat necrosis as a complication [7]. These do not concern the buttock.

General buttock surgery risks include infection, wound opening, seroma, asymmetry and anesthetic complications [2]. Fat necrosis is a recognised complication of fat-containing flaps in breast surgery, where it can mimic recurrence and affect cosmetic results [7].

timeline.event: A dermal-fat flap is described for nipple reconstruction, an early reconstructive use of the tissue type [8].
A remodeling body lift using a dermal fat flap and tissue suspension is published [6].
Autologous augmentation gluteoplasty with a dermal fat flap is reported in 10 patients [1].
